subject.title: [Feature]: muteKeywords channel config — drop messages matching keyword/regex list before agent dispatch

question: Should OpenClaw add a regex-capable `muteKeywords` channel config surface, and should it be a shared channel contract or separate plugin-owned Slack/Discord fields?
rationale: The request is useful but creates a new operator config and intentional message-drop behavior; repository policy treats new config/drop surfaces as compatibility-sensitive and current code has only narrower mention gates.

options.title: Approve a narrow design first
options.body: Define safe literal/regex parsing, invalid-pattern behavior, history recording, and Slack/Discord ownership before inviting a focused implementation PR.

options.title: Decline the new config surface
options.body: Keep existing `requireMention`, `mentionPatterns`, `ignoreOtherMentions`, `allowBots`, and bot-loop controls as the supported noise-reduction tools.

options.title: Move to plugin/API design
options.body: Ask for a broader channel-plugin filtering seam only if maintainers want third-party or per-channel packages to own content filters outside bundled plugins.

recommendation.title: Approve a narrow design first
recommendation.body: Define safe literal/regex parsing, invalid-pattern behavior, history recording, and Slack/Discord ownership before inviting a focused implementation PR.

likelyOwner.reason: Recent channel/config hardening and repository-policy context make this the best available routing candidate from the inspected history.
